# Grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks

Grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks in the HMI library has 324 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Cu, Mn, Zn, V, Ba, Si and Ti from 14 sources.<sup For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-grain-based-snacks" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-grain-based-snacks-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤6</td><td>3.6–6.2 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤6.2</td><td>4.1–6.2 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>66 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>27</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Elsheikh et al. 2020</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2024</td><td>38</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li><li><a href="../sources/elsheikh2020-toxic-trace-elements-children-foods-infant-formulae-saudi" class="internal" data-slug="sources/elsheikh2020-toxic-trace-elements-children-foods-infant-formulae-saudi" data-no-cite-meta>Elsheikh et al. 2020</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024" data-no-cite-meta>U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2024</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="levers-to-reduce-contamination"></a>

<a id="testing-grain-based-snacks-crackers-biscuits-cookies-popcorn-pretzels--non-rice-clean-counterpart-to-rice-snacks-for-metals"></a>
<a id="sampling-testing-and-verification"></a>
## Testing grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks for metals

<a id="hmi-prd-022"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-needed-for-lot-decisions-surveillance-and-verification-of-a-process-change"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-023"></a>
<a id="which-analytical-or-migrationrelease-methods-match-this-product-species-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-024"></a>
<a id="what-can-testing-and-supplier-coas-establish-about-a-lot-and-what-cannot-be-generalized-to-all-production"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 2 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 100 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Cu, Mn, Zn, V, Ba, Si and Ti in grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-grain-based-snacks-crackers-biscuits-cookies-popcorn-pretzels--non-rice-clean-counterpart-to-rice-snacks" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-grain-based-snacks-crackers-biscuits-cookies-popcorn-pretzels--non-rice-clean-counterpart-to-rice-snacks" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in EMRO (16 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (19 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For inorganic arsenic, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (9 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (83 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-grain-based-snacks-crackers-biscuits-cookies-popcorn-pretzels--non-rice-clean-counterpart-to-rice-snacks-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-grain-based-snacks-crackers-biscuits-cookies-popcorn-pretzels--non-rice-clean-counterpart-to-rice-snacks-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in grain-based snacks (crackers, biscuits, cookies, popcorn, pretzels) — non-rice clean counterpart to rice-snacks is inorganic?">

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 8 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span
